component_postures.basis: USDA Grain Transportation Report documented VLSFO near $960/metric ton on March 11, up 79% in two weeks, and IFO 380 reaching an all-time high March 9.
USDA documented higher U.S. Gulf-to-Japan and Pacific Northwest-to-Japan grain ocean freight rates during the same shock interval.
BLS March PPI documented a 42.0% monthly increase in No. 2 diesel fuel within processed intermediate demand.
BLS recorded March transportation/warehousing price pressure and USDA later documented materially higher rail fuel surcharges tied to diesel cost conditions.

Nationwide CPI food was flat month over month in March, then rose in subsequent months; this supports later consumer-food movement but not sole attribution to shipping fuel. Importantly, the March nationwide food-at-home index remained 1.9% above its year-earlier level despite a -0.2% seasonally adjusted monthly move, so no household-affordability improvement is inferred.

Under the frozen nationwide CPI-U monthly consumer-category comparator and primary March 9-11 marine-fuel-shock clock, food was not uniquely the first category to show monthly movement. This is a narrow ordering result only: the national food-at-home index was still 1.9% above March 2025 and the result does not imply grocery bills or household purchasing power improved.
Current preserved first-party text does not authorize an exclusivity claim, and observed food prices have multiple contemporaneous causal inputs.

affordability_guard: A monthly CPI decrease cannot be translated into improved household grocery affordability or purchasing power without separate price-level, wage/income, geography, and household-basket evidence.
component_resolution_rule: Supported intermediate transition links may receive component support without converting the terminal forecast into RESOLVED_CORRECT; a failed terminal ordering component likewise does not erase supported intermediate mechanism links.
next_gate: Preserve any retrievable March 18 transcript to determine whether the video narrows, broadens, or qualifies the subtitle-level ordering claim. Until then, the V1 CPI ordering result is binding only for the explicitly bounded nationwide monthly CPI interpretation.
